judgment.rationale: The visible warning is expected while PowerToys is elevated, but the report does not prove whether the process remains elevated after a full exit and normal restart. Without that distinction, designing a code fix would risk solving the intentional WinUI drag/drop safeguard instead of any startup-elevation defect.

The reporter states disabling the Run as administrator toggle did not restore layout editing, but no full tray-exit/restart elevation check or diagnostic archive is present.
MouseWithoutBordersViewModel.cs sets DeviceViewModel.CanDragDrop to !IsElevated, and MouseWithoutBordersPage.xaml binds AllowDrop and CanDrag to that property.
The source comment points to a WinUI elevated-drag crash workaround; this makes the layout lock intentional while elevated.

inferences: The current process may still have elevated rights because changing the setting cannot de-elevate an already-running process.

comment.body: Thanks for the clear PowerToys 0.101.2362 report and exact Mouse Without Borders warning. The layout editor intentionally disables WinUI drag-and-drop while the running PowerToys process is elevated, and turning off the setting does not lower an already-running process. Please fully exit PowerToys from the tray, confirm in Task Manager that no PowerToys processes remain, restart normally with `Run as administrator` disabled, and tell us whether Task Manager still shows PowerToys as elevated. If it still starts elevated, reproduce the locked layout once and then add a comment containing `/bugreport` immediately so the generated ZIP captures that startup state; please also mention any executable compatibility setting or organizational policy that forces PowerToys to run as administrator.
